info.description: Every node is a new discovery. The JSON API under `/api/v1` (architecture §9): errors are always the `Error` envelope, and every path but the auth ones and this document needs the session cookie.

put.summary:

hid), with no cap, and may be empty only when none is shown;
`409 stale_order` otherwise, so a reorder from an old page can't
drop or duplicate entries. Entries not shown to the client (Adult while
hidden, and filter-hidden ones it did not name) keep their slots.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The Newest tab: a content type (`movie`, `tv`, `music`,
`audiobook`, `ebook`, `comic`, `software`, `game`, `images`,
`video`, `other`, `adult`); absent is every type.

get.summary: The live event stream.
get.description:
Each frame is `id: <epoch>-<seq>` (none on `resync`), `event: <name>`
and `data: <json>`, the payload of the `Event` variant of that name.
Send the last id back as `Last-Event-ID` (`EventSource` does) to
replay what was missed; when that can't be done exactly (a restart,
too long ago, or an id that isn't ours), a `resync` comes first. A
client that falls behind gets a `resync` and carries on from live. A
comment every 15 s keeps the connection open; `retry:` is 5 s.

parameters.name: topics
parameters.description:
Comma-separated topics, e.g. `torrents,crawler`; all of them when
absent. An unknown or empty one is a 400 with `field: "topics"`.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last `id:` received, to resume after it.

200.description: The stream: one `Event` per frame (`event:` names the variant, `data:` holds its payload).

X-Accel-Buffering.description: `no`, so a proxy doesn't buffer it.

429.description: Too many open streams, in all or for this session (`too_many_streams`).

503.description: Not served here, or shutting down (`events_unavailable`).

post.summary:
Cancels a job: it stops at its next step (a paused one at once). A
cancelled export's download ends with an error, so it's never taken
for a complete file.

Pauses a job: it stops at its next step and holds nothing while it
waits (an export's download waits too). Unless it's resumed within
10 minutes it fails with `pause_expired`. Pausing a paused job does
nothing.
Resumes a paused job. Resuming a running job does nothing.

get.summary: The live log.
get.description:
Each frame is `id: <epoch>-<seq>` (none on `resync` and `purge`),
`event: line | resync | purge` and `data:` its payload (`LogFrame`).
Send the last id back as `Last-Event-ID` (`EventSource` does) or
`after` to resume without a gap while it's still in the ring. A comment
every 15 s keeps the connection open, and the session is checked again
each time; `retry:` is 5 s.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The least severe level shown: error, warn, info, debug or trace (default).

parameters.name: components
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of components (`LogComponent`); all when absent.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: A case-insensitive substring of the line as shown, at most 200 characters.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The id to resume after, when there's no `Last-Event-ID`.

200.description: The stream: one `LogFrame` per frame (`event:` names the variant, `data:` holds its payload).

X-Accel-Buffering.description: `no`, so a proxy doesn't buffer it.

401.description: No session (`login_required`); keys and feed tokens can't read logs.

429.description: Too many log streams, in all or for this session (`too_many_streams`).

get.summary:
The fields the query language accepts: name, aliases, value type,
operators, fixed values and whether `/facets` counts it. With "Show
adult content" off, `adult:` and `type:adult` aren't listed (§20.9).
It doesn't need the index, so it answers while search is off.

post.summary:
Registers a live query: the count of new matches for `q` (or `ast`)
arrives as `search_live` events on `/events`, to this session only.
post.description:
The query is validated and bounded as `/search` bounds it, and runs
with the same visibility: torrents a filter rule hid unless `hidden`,
and no Adult while "Show adult content" is off. Changing that setting
releases every live query: register again. A session holds at most 4
(a fifth replaces the oldest); one is released 30 s after the
session's last `/events` connection closes (a reconnect keeps it),
after 60 s if no connection opens, on a `content` settings save,
or with `DELETE /search/live/{id}`. Register again after a `settings`
event for `content`, or when a `search_live` id you hold is no longer
known (a 404 on `DELETE`). Swarm clauses (`seeders:`…) match nothing
at index time, so a query with one counts only what it can see then.
Where the percolator doesn't run (fixture mode), nothing is counted.
Any `/events` connection of the session keeps its registrations, whatever
its `topics`.

429.description: Too many live queries are registered (`too_many_live_queries`).

503.description: Search is off (`search_disabled`), or live updates aren't served (`events_unavailable`).

change. Keys that aren't settings, read-only ones, secrets and ones an
environment variable sets are listed in `skipped` and left alone.

LAN; notification channels never on loopback; nothing on link-local,
metadata or reserved addresses). A secret the form leaves out is the
saved one, only while the address is on the saved server. Nothing is
saved, and the result never repeats the URL, a credential or what the
server answered.

are listed in `restart_required`. A field an environment variable
sets is refused, naming the variable. With `if_revision`, a section

Every source plugin of this build: kind, consent class, stored state,
priority and health.

patch.summary:
Enables or disables a source, or sets its priority. A priority
applies at once; enabling or disabling at the next start.
patch.description:
This build turns on only a source whose class is `none`. Enabling an
`external`, `account`, `restricted` or `overlay` source is refused with
`400 invalid_setting` on `enabled`, before its consent, acknowledgement
or credentials are looked at, whatever the request sends: this version
can't show the class's consent dialog yet. A `"password"` sent with the
enable is still checked first (`401` when it's wrong). `needs` and
`credential_spec` still say what the source will need once a later
version can turn it on, and credentials can be stored and removed
meanwhile (`PATCH /sources/{id}/credentials`). Disabling works for every
class.

Agents, egress and the schedule apply at the next start; changing
egress needs the admin `"password"` (`428 confirm_required`), and the
`interface` and `bind_address` routes are refused (`409
route_unavailable`). `config` sets the source's settings, for a source
whose `editable` lists it: a JSON object of at most 16 KiB, shaped by
its `config_schema`, that the source's own rules check (`400
invalid_config` names the rule, never a value). It applies at the next
start; a torrent cache whose new list holds an address its
acknowledgement doesn't is switched off there. A purge isn't a field:
it's `POST /sources/{id}/purge` (`409 not_editable` here).

parameters.name: id

patch.summary:
Stores or removes a source's credentials: each name maps to a value
(stored, sealed with the install's key) or `null` (removed). Values
are never returned: the response lists the names stored. Removing what
an enabled `account` source needs disables it. `400
invalid_credentials` names the rule a change broke, never a value.

parameters.name: id

state, its credentials, consent record and settings, and their copies

with progress, pause and cancel. It needs the admin `"password"`
every time (`428 confirm_required`, `401`): it can't be undone.

The source is turned off first. A purge that stops partway (cancelled,
failed, or cut short by a restart) keeps what it did and the source
off (`purge_pending` in `GET /sources`); purging again finishes it.
`409 purge_running` while one runs for this source.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The source's id, as `GET /sources` lists it.

(§10.10.7). It changes nothing: the source keeps its state, data,
credentials and settings, and no job starts. It needs a session, like
every Sources route, and no password: the password is asked once, by
`POST /sources/{id}/purge`. The counts are exact while the source is
off (`settled`); see `PurgePreview`.

parameters.name: id

The build, this installation, the restart and any pending address

Keeps the new HTTP address: this process is serving on it, so the
request itself shows it's reachable (whatever `Host` says: a reverse
proxy may rewrite it). `409 no_address_change` unless one is awaiting
confirmation.

Goes back to the previous HTTP address now. Awaiting confirmation,
the previous value is saved again and the server restarts onto it
(`restarting`); awaiting the restart, the saved change is undone and
nothing restarts. `409 no_address_change` when there's no change.

Restarts Lodestar: a graceful shutdown (the queue, DHT state and last
commit are saved), then the same program again. It answers first;
poll `/healthz` until it's back. `409 restart_unavailable` where it
can't restart itself, with how to restart instead; `409
restart_failed` when it couldn't get ready to (the portable build
couldn't start its new copy), and it keeps running.

409.description: `restart_unavailable`: restart it the way it was started (the message says how). `restart_failed`: it couldn't get ready to restart (the portable build couldn't start its new copy), so it's still running.

are kept (`rollback.available` in `GET /updates`). It runs the same
journal as `lodestar rollback`: Lodestar shuts down gracefully, the
supervisor rolls back (restoring the store when the update migrated
it) and starts the previous version, which never installs the
rolled-back one automatically again. Revocations are kept.

No password yet: claim the instance with the setup token from the

Items read per second (`done` and `skipped`), paused time left

Items left out: for an export, torrents it may not include
(withheld, private-source, deleted or unknown), counted without
saying which or why.

What a job does. `import` is reserved for the importer framework
(§18.8): nothing starts one yet, but the Jobs view can render it.
`purge` removes a source's data (`POST /sources/{id}/purge`).

Where a job is. `running` and `paused` hold one of the running

Blocked.description: One reason a release doesn't install automatically.

commit.description: The full commit hash; null when the build didn't know it.

date.description:
Unix seconds: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, else the commit's date; null
when neither was known (never the time of the build, so builds
stay reproducible).

rustc.description: `rustc -V` of the compiler that built it.

ui_build_id.description:
The embedded UI's build id (SvelteKit's `_app/version.json`); null
when the binary embeds the stub page.

Capability.description: Whether this installation can install updates itself.

reason.description:
Why not: `not_supervised`, `dev_build`, `noexec`, `not_writable`,
`package_managed`, `image_mode`, `trust_damaged`,
`skipped_unreadable`, `noexec_unknown`, `channel_unavailable` or
`not_built_yet` (Windows: this install path isn't built yet, e.g.
the portable build, or no installer wired in); on Windows also
`install_kind_unknown` (Lodestar couldn't tell whether it's the MSI
service or the portable zip, so no artifact is chosen) and
`data_folder_unchecked` (the data folder isn't the default one
under ProgramData whose permissions the installer sets, so nothing
installs from it); or, when `unavailable` is
set, the same reason (`fixture`, `network`, `windows_helper`).
Install automatically then behaves as Check and notify.

CatalogList.description:
A list in the one-click catalog. Send `url`, `kind` and `format` as a
`subscribe` change to connect it.

about.description: What it blocks, in plain language.

figures.description: Its catalog measurement, or its own data once connected.

subscription.description: The subscription's id once you connected it.

oneOf.description: A pack (`malware`) or one pack rule (`MW-2`).

unless.description: An empty string removes the clause.

oneOf.description:
Your override of one pack rule (RP-2): its action, and optionally
an `unless`. It never changes what the rule matches, and it replaces
the rule's override if it has one. Any `unless`, or an action lighter
than what applies now, weakens filtering: confirm it with the
password and send back the assessment's [`Assessment::pack_base`]
as `base`. The override is bound to that version; once a newer
version is accepted, one that weakens the new version pauses until
it's set again.

base.description: The previewed `pack_base`, to confirm a weakening override.

oneOf.description:
Removes your override of one pack rule: the rule applies as built.
Removing one heavier than the rule's own action weakens filtering.

Confirms again your override of one pack rule whose base changed
since you set it (RP-3, §20.8): the same action and `unless`, bound
to the version that applies now. Confirming one that weakens the
rule as it is now (a paused one, among them) needs the password and
the assessment's [`Assessment::pack_base`] sent back as `base`.

base.description: The previewed `pack_base`, to confirm a weakening override.

oneOf.description:
Accepts the pending versions of pack rules (RP-3, §20.10): each
named rule (`MW-2`), or every pending rule of a named pack
(`malware`), switches to the version this build ships. Nothing is
released: holds the new version wouldn't make stay for review.

It strengthens filtering only when every accepted version's
recorded direction is `widens` or `action-heavier` and the shadow
results agree. Anything else weakens it: confirm with the password
and send back the assessment's [`Assessment::pack_versions`] as
`versions`. Undo never undoes an acceptance.

versions.description:
The previewed `pack_versions` (`RULE@version`), to confirm a
weakening acceptance. When sent, apply accepts only exactly
these.

oneOf.description: Report torrents as child-abuse material (§20.5.2).

A quarantined torrent a rule caught wrongly (§20.12): an exception
for that torrent and that rule only, a hashed must-not-match
fixture for a core rule, and a release.

Releases a quarantined or dropped torrent: fetched and processed
normally next time it's seen.

Confirms a quarantined torrent as abuse material: into CS-1, sealed
name deleted.

Accepts or discards a version the sanity gates held back.

Accepting one that drops entries is weakening, so it's confirmed
with the password for the version the warning described: send back
the assessment's [`Assessment::held_version`] as `held`. A refresh
that holds another version in between makes apply refuse with 409
`changed_since_preview`.

Settles floor entries a config file or a floor-marked list dropped
(owner's decision §2.7). They stay blocked until this: `remove`
takes them out of the floor, which weakens it; otherwise they stay
in it as ordinary CS-1b entries. `source` is a pending source's key
(`file:<path>`, `list:<id>`).

A removal confirmed with the password must name its entries: send
back the assessment's [`Assessment::floor_entries`], so the
password confirms what the warning listed. Keeping may leave
`hashes` out, which keeps what the assessment counted.

Change.description: One change to filtering (§20.7), tagged by `op`.

ChangeBody.description:
`POST /filters/preview`, `/filters/preview/jobs` and `/filters/apply`.
`Debug` shows whether a password was sent, never the password.

password.description:
The admin password, for a change that weakens filtering (§20.11);
ignored by previews.

source.description:
Where a setting's effective value comes from, lowest to highest:
the built-in default, `config.toml`, a change saved in the app, or a
`LODESTAR_*` environment variable.

direction.description:
`widens`, `narrows`, `action-heavier`, `action-lighter` or `mixed`

text.description: The entry's text (Markdown); null when the changelog has none.

A range of characters (Unicode scalar values) in the query, end

checked_at.description: Unix seconds of the last completed check.

next_check_at.description: When the next scheduled check runs; null when updates are off.

What a source claimed that the verified metadata contradicts

oneOf.description:
Files claimed against files in the info dictionary (padding
excluded).
Both names are cut to 1,024 bytes.
Bytes.

ClaimedText.description: A claimed text and the verified one.

queued.description:
Stored torrents queued to be classified again; null without a

More stored torrents matched than are queued at once (1,000,000):

query.description: Can't test `type:` or `adult:`: the rule decides them.

Classes.description:
`GET /classify`: your classification rules, and how detection

ClauseRemoval.description: One top-level clause and what the query gives without it.

The clause's position among the AST's top-level clauses, as the

Matches without the clause. Absent when the shared deadline passed

`total` is an estimate, by the same rule as `/search`'s

When refused: `not_found` (unknown, or withheld from you, which

position.description:
1-based place among the entries shown, so it never reveals how
many were left out.

CollectionSummary.description: A collection. `items` counts the torrents search would show.

Companion.description: One companion: the list's row and the detail.

available.description:
The version an install or update would fetch here; null when it's
up to date or can't be installed here (`refusal` says why).

credentials.description:
The stored credentials, by field (`webui_password`, `api_key`):
names only, never values. What `…/reveal` can show.

oneOf.description: The last health check the manager saw.

health.description: Null when Lodestar didn't install it.

installed.description: The version Lodestar installed; null when it didn't.

refusal.description:
Why it can't be installed or updated here, as a stable code

`202` for a restart or a regenerated credential: the change is under
way; the companion's row says when it's done.

CompanionForgotten.description:
What forgetting a companion you added deleted: Lodestar's record of it
and its stored credential, by `settings` key. The download client entry
in Integrations stays.

credential_in_use.description:
The deleted credential was one Lodestar generated, which is, or may
be, the password qBittorrent uses now. Reveal it before forgetting
if you'll need to sign in to qBittorrent yourself.

CompanionInstallRequest.description:
`POST /companions/{id}/install`: the offer's version and SHA-256,

CompanionPasteRequest.description:
`POST /companions/{id}/paste`: qBittorrent's temporary WebUI password
(Q19), sealed at once and never shown again.

CompanionPlan.description:
The settings a configuration changes, by name (never a value), shown
before you confirm.

oneOf.description:
Its catalogue container name, on Docker's network (only when
Lodestar runs in a container).

CompanionTarget.description:
Where a companion is: loopback or Docker's network on one of its
catalogue ports, or an address you typed (`http`/`https`, no user name
or password, query or fragment).

compose.description: The compose document, for `kind: compose`; null otherwise.

unraid.description:
gluetun's template first when it's generated, then the
companion's, for `kind: unraid`; empty otherwise.

hashes.description: 2–5 distinct 40-character hex info hashes, in column order.

For each parsed attribute any torrent has (the release fields:
`title`, `year`, `res`, `vcodec`, `group`, …), whether the values
differ across the set. A torrent without the attribute counts as
a different value.

scale_bytes.description:
The shared scale for the composition bars: the largest `size` of
the set, in bytes.

torrents.description: One per hash, in the request's order.

Every attribute in `differs`: this torrent's value, or null when

Whole percent of the non-padding bytes: any non-zero share is at
least 1, and only a complete one is 100.

pct_files.description: The same, of the non-padding files.

`POST /sessions/revoke-others`, and any other change that only needs
the password (§20.11). `Debug` redacts it.

The admin password, every time. Without it the answer is 428
`confirm_required`.

ConnectedList.description: One of your lists and its own figures.

held.description:
A version the sanity gates held back waits for *Accept anyway*
or *Keep previous* (`resolve_held`).

How many are enabled (sources, lists, integrations); null for the

last_checked_at.description:
Unix seconds of the last contact, where it's recorded (a list's

settings.description: The Settings screen that changes it (`/settings/<screen>`).

Null for what this build doesn't have yet (updates until the

floor.description: Part of the locked floor: can't be switched off.

`POST /classify/correct`: your correction to one stored torrent,

When relabelling it adult made filtering hold it back (§20.9): the

`event: crawler`: the same counters as the status page and

Nodes in the DHT routing table; null when the DHT is off or

The crawler is paused (`POST /crawler/pause`): the counters stand

something broke.

The environment variable that sets the intensity, which then

hidden.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3), as `/search`.

lease.description:
A search response's `next_cursor`: count the same index snapshot
as its results. Send the same `q`, `sort` and `hidden` with it.
Without one, the index serving now.

limits.description: Values listed per facet: 8 by default, 1–100.

q.description:
The query text, as `/search` takes it. Send `q` or `ast`, not
both.

sort.description:
The search's sort; it doesn't change the counts, but a `lease`
is checked against it.

tz.description:
The user's zone for `time:`, in minutes east of UTC (−840 to
840), as `/search`; 0 by default.

FacetsResponse.description:
`GET`/`POST /facets`. Counts are disjunctive: a facet's counts ignore
the query's own clauses on that facet (architecture §16, "B6").

backfill_before.description:
When the crawler first ran (Unix seconds); discovered bins that
end by then are `backfill`. Null when the store doesn't know.

buckets.description:
The swarm buckets: null until swarm health is in the index (M4),
never zeros.

canonical.description: The query as the server understood it.

facets.description:
Term facets by name: `type`, `ext`, `res`, `category`, `lang`,
`group`, `codec`, `audio`, `hdr`, `private`, `v2`, `has`,
`ambiguous`, `imported`, `backfill`, `network`, `source`,
`verified`, and `adult` when there are adult subtypes to list.

`verified` counts `no` even while the search hides unverified
items, since its default `verified:yes` is the facet's own
selection; `source` lists plugin ids (names in `source_names`),
and never a private source's to anyone but the admin session
(§18.7).

sample_rate.description:
The share of the documents a sampled group visited (for the "≈"
note); null when nothing was sampled.

sampled.description:
Some group was computed on a sample (above 1,000,000 matches, or
300,000 when a segment holds more than 300,000 torrents).

source_names.description: The display name of each plugin id the `source` facet lists.

total.description: The search's result count, as `/search` reports it.

unavailable.description:
Groups this index can't serve: fields an older index lacks while
it's rebuilt, and the swarm buckets until M4.

fetch_latency_p50_ms.description:
Fetch latency percentiles. Null until a fetch latency histogram
exists.

fetched.description:
Info dicts fetched in the range, by event time; null when the range
starts before they were counted so.

limiter_rejections.description: Per-IP limiter rejections. Null until counted.

lost.description:
Keys lost in the range (with `reason`, for that reason only), by
event time; null as `fetched`.

mse_share.description: MSE (encrypted) share of successful fetches. Null until counted.

queue_age_s.description: Age of the oldest queued key. Null until the pool reports it.

queue_depth.description: Keys queued or in flight now. Snapshot.

utp_share.description: uTP share of successful fetches. Null until counted.

by_worker.description:
Each worker's leases that ended, the built-in crawler (worker 0)
first (§19.7). Left out on a single machine. Counts only.

funnel.description:
The discovery-cohort funnel, as the overview's (with `reason`, only
that loss).

losses.description:
Losses by reason, by event time, most first; null when the range
starts before fetches were counted by event time.

reason.description: The `reason` filter, as asked; null for all.

queued.description: Keys waiting for a fetch slot or for peers.

FetchWorker.description: One worker on Fetch (WK-15): its leases that ended in the range.

committed.description: Results it fetched that were committed. Event time.

lost.description:
Keys it lost, for any reason (`reason` doesn't narrow it). Event
time.

worker.description: The worker's id; 0 is this server's own crawler.

FieldOperator.description: How a value is written after `name:`.

FieldPreview.description: One patched field, as it would be saved.

restart_required.description: It would apply at the next restart; otherwise at once.

value.description: The value it would have (null for a secret).

FileDiff.description:
The file lists compared: files match when their path (inside the
torrent, `/`-separated, decoded) and size are equal. Padding files
are left out.

common.description: Files every torrent has, in the first torrent's order.

only.description:
Per torrent, in the request's order: files no other torrent has.
With three or more torrents, a file some but not all have is in
neither list.

count.description: Files in the list in all, listed or not.

files.description: At most 2,000, in the torrent's order.

FilesPage.description: `GET /torrents/{hash}/files`: a page of the file list.

Fix.description: Where an exception's fix is: a settings section or a stage page.

kind.description:
`settings`, `stage` or `guide` (a page of the user guide). A
client offers no link for a kind it doesn't know.

target.description:
The section or stage (`index`, `fetch`, …), or the guide's topic:
`data_folder` (where to keep the data folder) or `windows_ports`
(the port range on Windows).

failing.description: Examples the rule now gets wrong.

Fixtures.description:
`GET /filters/fixtures`: the core rules' hashed examples, run against
the rules as they are, and the pack corpora (§20.8).

paused.description: Connected, taking no new work until resumed.

stored_per_hour.description:
Torrents the whole fleet (the coordinator's own crawler included)
newly stored in the last full UTC hour, as the overview's
`ingest_per_hour`; `null` when that hour wasn't measured.

workers.description:
Remote workers doing work now: `online` plus `draining` (the pill's
"3 workers").

oneOf.description:
`null` when no remote worker has joined: the pill shows nothing
new.

FunnelCohort.description: One discovery cohort (or a UTC day of them) in the funnel (§10.9.3).

cohort.description: The cohort's first hour, unix seconds.

final.description:
Final: nothing in progress and everything stored searchable, or
past the 72 h retry horizon. A day is final when all its hours
are. Not final is "incomplete" (hatched).

losses.description:
Losses by reason (`no_peers`, `timed_out`, `refused`,
`encryption_failed`, `oversize`, `invalid`, `blocked`, `evicted`,
`gave_up`, `unreachable`), every reason listed.

FunnelStages.description: Hashes of the cohort that reached each stage.

FunnelTotal.description: The funnel over every cohort in the range.

cohorts.description: Cohort hours in the range with any count.

loss_share.description:
Each reason's share of all losses, 0–1; null when nothing was
lost.

HashList.description:
A list of torrents by info hash: `POST /collections/{id}/items`,
`…/items/remove` and `PUT …/order`.

Health.description: Health (§10.9.2): running, paused or degraded, with the reason.

Histogram.description: A histogram with explicit bins; empty bins are present with count 0.

missing.description:
Matches without a value (no year parsed); the bins plus this sum
to the result count.

unit.description:
What the edges measure: `bytes`; `hour`, `day`, `week` (from a
Thursday), `month` or `year` in UTC seconds (`discovered`, whose
first and last bins may be irregular edge bins); or `year` (the
release year).

backfill.description: Ends by the crawler's first run (`backfill_before`).

hi.description: Exclusive; null for the open top bin.

HitGroup.description:
A section of result rows (the row search returns) that may not be
available in this build or for this torrent. Unavailable is never an
empty list that reads as "none": `status` says which.

oneOf.description: Why it's unavailable; null when available.

truncated.description: More matched than the group lists.

HitSource.description: A hit's source: the display name, and the id `source:` takes.

cpus.description: CPU cores this process may use.

memory_bytes.description:
Memory this process may use: the machine's, or a container's
limit when lower.

alt_titles.description: Other titles the work is known by, at most 32.

canonical_title.description: The work's own title in the plugin's database.

chosen.description:
The torrent's effective title is this answer's: its name said
nothing, and the record was resolved via a plugin with the surest
answer that has a canonical title. At most one answer is chosen;
none when the title isn't a plugin's, or the chosen answer's source
isn't shown to this caller.

confidence.description: How sure the plugin is of the match, 0–100 percent.

ids.description:
The work's ids, at most 32, in the closed schemes enrichment
writes: imdb, tmdb, tvdb, anidb, anilist, mbid, olid, igdb,
discogs, steam, wikidata.

source.description: The plugin that answered: "Identified by Wikidata".

IdentifiedAs.description:
What general enrichment plugins (Wikidata, TMDB, …) identified a
torrent as (ENR-10, ENR-12; architecture §6, §10.5). Every text was
judged by the content filter before it was stored, and nothing is
judged again here.

alternatives.description:
Each plugin's answer, the surest first (ties by source id). Two
plugins that disagree are both kept.

resolved_via.description:
How an ambiguous name's effective title was resolved, when it was
from the file tree: `files`, `folder` or `structure`. Null in every
other case: the name said it itself, the title came from a plugin
(see `chosen`), or the record can't be read. **Null never means
"from the name"**: don't present it as that.

alt_titles.title: ショーシャンクの空に

IdentifiedId.description: A work's id in one scheme.

IdentifiedTitle.description: An alternative title and its language.

language.description: A BCP 47 tag, lower case; `und` when the plugin didn't say.

from_source.description:
Where the value now comes from: to undo, send it back, or `null`
when this isn't `db`.

restart_required.description: It applies at the next restart.

ImportNote.description: What an import annotation says, so a step in the trend is explained.

merged.description:
`import_finished`: records the store already had, merged as
provenance only (already known). Null otherwise.

new.description:
`import_finished`: records the job stored new (novel). Null
otherwise.

removed.description: `import_removed`: torrents the removal deleted. Null otherwise.

ImportReport.description: `POST /settings/import`: the diff, and whether it was applied.

applied.description: Saved (false on a dry run, or when nothing changes).

revisions.description:
Every section's revision after the import: pass them back with
the real import to refuse it if anything changed after a dry run.

unchanged.description: Settings in the file that already have its value.

ImportSkip.description: A key in the file that an import leaves alone.

env.description: The variable that sets it, for `set_by_environment`; null otherwise.

key.description: `section.field`, or the key as the file has it.

data_bytes.description: Bytes in the data directory. Snapshot.

disk_free_bytes.description: Free bytes on its volume: always null in this build.

file_index_coverage.description: File-index coverage (smart mode). Null until measured.

merges.description: Segment merges. Null until the index reports them.

new_searchable.description:
Crawled torrents that became searchable in the range, imports
excluded. Event time.

new_searchable_imported.description: Imported torrents that became searchable in the range. Event time.

projection_days.description: Days until the disk is full. Null while free space is unknown.

rebuild.description:
A background rebuild's phase (`building`, `finishing`, `swapping`,
`failed`); null when none runs. Snapshot.

removed.description: Searchable torrents deleted in the range. Event time.

scrape_coverage.description: Share of torrents with a swarm row. Null until rolled up.

scrape_freshness_s.description: Median age of scrape data. Null until rolled up.

searchable.description: Documents in the index now; null with search off. Snapshot.

segments.description: Index segments now. Null until the index reports them.

oneOf.description:
Database, index and file-index sizes against the §3 budget. Null
until each part is measured.

searchable.description:
The bucket's last searchable snapshot (a gauge: the last hour's);
null with none.

IndexRebuild.description:
A rebuild's progress, as `event: rebuild` sends it, with when it
started.

done.description: Torrents in the new index so far.

unavailable.description: Fields that match nothing until the swap.

removed_by_type.description:
Searchable torrents deleted in the range (a lifecycle event,
§10.9.3), by content type, Adult left out while hidden. Event time.

trackers.description: Per-tracker health. Null until it's rolled up.

by_ip_family.description: Yield by IPv4 / IPv6. Null until leases carry the address family.

by_source.description:
Keys reported, rediscovered and dropped, by the source that
reported them. Event time.

by_strategy.description:
Keys reported, by harvest strategy: the DHT's (BEP 51 sample,
get_peers, announce, lookup), refetch, and each other source's own
codes. Event time: volume, not yield.

by_worker.description:
Each worker's keys, the built-in crawler (worker 0) first, then
remote workers by id (§19.7). Left out on a single machine, where
no worker has counted anything. Counts only.

InsightsEvent.description:
`event: insights`, every 30 s while anyone subscribes: the default
`7d` overview's stage strip (`docs/metrics.md` §6.1, §7.5, §7.7). A
client showing another range refetches its own on each event.

InsightsException.description: An exception (§10.9.2 level 5): text + icon + a fix action.

oneOf.description:
`filter_stand_ins_rejudged` only: what's still held, and what was
made while the rows couldn't be read and is left for you to review.
`data_filesystem` only: what holds the data folder.

kind.description:
`index_lag` (the index more than 30 s behind), `cohort_stalled`
(hashes in progress, the crawler running, and nothing stored for
2 full hours), `yield_below_baseline`, or `filter_rows_unreadable`
(stored filter rows that no longer read; filtering fails closed
for them until they're fixed in Filters & Safety), or
`filter_stand_ins_rejudged` (for a week after such rows read
again: `value` torrents their stand-ins held were released, and
`counts` has the rest), `data_filesystem` (the data folder is on
Unraid's user share, another FUSE filesystem or a network share;
`filesystem` says which), or `ephemeral_ports` (Windows has too
few ports left for outgoing connections; `value` ports are left
and `ports` has the fix). The last two are checked at most hourly.
A client shows a kind it doesn't know generically.

oneOf.description: `ephemeral_ports` only: the port range and the fix.

rows.description:
The rows an exception is about, as the Filters & Safety screens
name them (`U-3`, `C-2`, …); empty for the other kinds.

unit.description:
`s`, `torrents`, `ratio`, `rows` or `ports`; null when the kind
has no number (`data_filesystem`).

InsightsHistogramBin.description: One bin of a distribution (parser confidence, junk score).

InsightsRange.description:
The range as the server normalized it: whole UTC hours, or whole UTC
days past 7 days.

to.description: Unix seconds, exclusive. The current hour (day) counts so far.

tz.description: The time zone buckets are in: always `UTC`.

fetch.description:
Null when the range starts before fetches were counted by event
time.

serve.description: Null until the search counters exist.

InstallOffer.description:
What an install or update would fetch, shown before you confirm it.
The confirmation echoes `version` and `sha256` exactly.

replaces.description: The installed version this update replaces; null for an install.

sha256.description: The pinned SHA-256 of the download, 64 lowercase hex digits.

InstallRequest.description:
`POST /updates/install`. A release with manual steps needs
`confirm_manual: true` (the steps are in its notes), else
`422 manual_confirmation_required`.

Installing.description: An install under way or queued for the window.

Integration.description: An app that can call in.

JobStatus.description:
`GET /filters/preview/jobs/{id}`: progress while it runs, then the
assessment or the error.

error.description: Once `failed`: the error the preview would have returned.

JoinCommands.description:
Ready-to-copy ways to join with the token (§19.6). Most hold the
token, so they're shown once with it. `Debug` redacts every one.

cli.description:
`lodestar worker`, given the token on standard input. The token is
in the line, so it lands in the shell's history; it's single use
and expires in 15 minutes. `cli_read` keeps it out.

cli_read.description:
The same, reading the token from a hidden prompt (`read -rs`):
paste the token when asked. Nothing secret is in the line.

docker_run.description:
A `docker run` line. Remove `LODESTAR_TOKEN` once the worker has
joined (it's spent; the worker warns about it at each start).

unraid.description: What to enter in the Unraid "Lodestar Worker" template.

windows.description:
What to enter in the Windows installer's "Join an existing
Lodestar".

KeyInfo.description: A key or token as listed: never its secret or hash.

last_used_at.description: Unix seconds, written at most once a minute; null: never used.

prefix.description: The secret's public start, to tell keys apart.

saved_search_id.description: A feed token's saved search; null: every feed (or an API key).

KeyScope.description: What a key may reach (see `keys::scope`). A route opts in to one.

imported.description:
Searchable torrents that were imported (bitmagnet import), part of
`searchable`; null until Insights' state is read at start.

new_searchable.description:
Crawled torrents that first became searchable in the range:
imports excluded (`new_searchable_imported`). Event time; 0 is
real.

new_searchable_imported.description:
Imported torrents that first became searchable in the range (an
import's records, indexed). Event time; 0 is real.

searchable.description: Documents in the search index now; null when search is off.

searchable_crawled.description:
Of `searchable`, the crawled ones: `searchable` less `imported`;
null when either is null.

searchable_delta.description:
The change since the previous period's end: now's count less
`previous.kpi.searchable`. Null without `compare=1`, for `all`,
with search off, or with no snapshot from then.

time_to_searchable_p50_delta_s.description:
`time_to_searchable_p50_s` less the previous period's, seconds;
null without `compare=1` or when either side is null.

time_to_searchable_p50_s.description:
First harvest → searchable, p50 and p95 seconds over the final
cohorts in the range. Always approximate (log buckets ≤ 10%).
Null when no cohort in the range is final.

yield.description:
Searchable ÷ harvested over the final cohorts in the range, 0–1.
Imports excluded. Null when no cohort in the range is final.

yield_delta.description:
`yield` less the previous period's, in ratio points (−1 to 1); null
without `compare=1` or when either side is null.

LegalNotice.description: `GET /legal/notice`: the Legal Notice this build shows.

text.description:
The notice as Markdown (headings, paragraphs, lists, bold, italics,
code and links), in English only.

version.description:
Raised only when the notice changes in substance; send it back to
accept.

example.text:
# Lodestar Legal Notice and Network Risks

**Version 5 · 2026-11-11**

Lodestar shows this notice before first use.

## 1. Who publishes Lodestar
- The **AGPL** lets you run, study, change and share it.
- Open an issue at https://github.com/dvortsis/lodestar-v2.

now.description: The server's clock (Unix seconds): deadlines are set from it.

LogComponent.description:
Where an event comes from (§12.1's per-component levels; `system` is
the process's own: start, stop, settings, logging).

LogDataKind.description:
A kind of data a line may contain (§12.1). `peer_activity` and
`filter_changes` are the opt-ins.

default_on.description:
On in the default preset (Normal). One that's off by default joins
at Detailed.

help_key.description: The message key of one line of help.

kinds.description: The data kinds it can carry (the badges).

label_key.description: The message key of its plain name ("Each failed metadata fetch").

oneOf.description: On only while this opt-in is.

rate_per_hour.description:
Lines per hour since start, from its counter, which counts while
it's off too.

LogField.description: One field of a log line.

LogFieldKind.description:
What a field of a log line carries: a data kind, an error (its kind,
and its message only for plain error types), a label the code wrote, or
a field of a line the code didn't type.

details.description:
Written while a data kind that identifies torrents or people, or
an opt-in, was on: "Contains torrent details".

opt_in.description: Written while an opt-in was on.

to.description: Its rotation time, or for the current file its last line.

LogFileState.description: Whether file logging is writing now.

folder.description: The logs folder; null when there's none to read.

index_readable.description:
`false`: the folder's details index couldn't be read, so every file
counts as having details.

LogFrame.description:
One frame of `GET /logs/stream`: `event:` names the variant, `data:`
holds its payload.

LogHistory.description: `GET /logs`: a page of history, newest first.

more.description:
More may be older than this page (a page cut short by the read cap
says so too).

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; null at the end.

unreadable.description:
Lines skipped because they were over 1 MiB or not the file's JSON
shape.

LogKind.description: One data kind and its switch.

identifying.description: Identifies torrents or people: turning it on is time-limited.

opt_in.description:
Only by opt-in, for at most 24 hours, never by a preset, never on
the console or the Event Log.

until.description: When it turns off: 0 off, -1 until turned off, else Unix seconds.

LogKindOutputs.description: Whether a kind shows on each output.

LogLevel.description: A level, from the least to the most verbose.

LogLine.description:
One log line, as the live log, the history and the stream show it:
through the data kinds in force now.

event.description: The catalogued event's id; null for a line the code didn't type.

id.description: `<epoch>-<seq>`; null for a line an older build wrote.

oneOf.description: The opt-in the line belongs to: when it turns off, the line goes.
A summary of folded lines.

target.description: The `tracing` target of a line the code didn't type.

truncated.description:
A value was cut to fit the ring's per-line limit (16 KiB); the
file has it whole.

LogOutputName.description: An output (§12.1): each has its own level and data kinds.

LogPurge.description:
`event: purge`: data kinds turned off. In lines up to `through`, set
those kinds' values to `[hidden]`, and drop lines whose `opt_in` is
listed.

through.description: The id of the newest line it applies to.

LogRepeated.description:
A fold summary: identical lines that came within the window after the
first one, counted rather than written.

first.description: The id of the first line, when the output gave it one.

LogResync.description:
`event: resync`: continue from the newest lines; reload `GET /logs`
for what was skipped.

evicted.description:
Lines that left the ring unseen (whether they matched is unknown);
`lagged` only.

skipped.description:
Matching lines skipped, still readable through `GET /logs`;
`lagged` only.

LogResyncReason.description: Why the live log asks the client to catch up.

LogValue.description:
A field's value as shown: text (`[hidden]`, `ref:…` or the value), a
number or a flag.

share.description: Of all losses in the range.

MatchInput.description:
What an override, exception or allow entry matches, as sent: exactly
one of the four.

NaturalChip.description: One recognised clause and the words it came from.

NaturalProposal.description:
What natural phrasing proposes (§10.4): recognised words become
clauses, and every other word stays as text.

canonical.description: The proposed query; it always parses back to `ast`.

chips.description: The recognised clauses, in the order they appear.

NetworkCheck.description:
`GET /network/check` and `POST /network/check`: the first-run
wizard's network check and the dashboard's "reachable" flag. Every
probe is ordinary DHT traffic; no outside service is asked (§18.7).

inbound_queries.description: DHT queries received in the window; null until measuring.

mapping.description: UPnP / NAT-PMP port mapping (§5). This build has neither.

min_window_s.description: `reachable` stays null until the window has run this long.

reachable.description:
Whether unsolicited inbound DHT queries arrive on the DHT port;
null is unknown.

unsolicited_queries.description: Of `inbound_queries`, the ones from nodes we hadn't sent anything to lately.

unsolicited_sources.description:
The distinct networks (/24 or /64) those came from, counting at
most the 64 most recent; null until measuring. `reachable` needs
at least 3.

window_s.description: The longest stretch of evidence looked at.

window_started_at.description:
Unix seconds the window started (bootstrap or a restart); null
before bootstrap.

NewestSection.description:
Discover's Newest: a page of result rows by `discovered_at`, newest
first, paged like search.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

notices.description:
As search's: `adult_hidden` for the `adult` tab while "Show adult
content" is off, so it's empty.

total.description: Searchable torrents in this tab, not just this page.

type.description: The tab; null is every type.

NtfyDraft.description:
An ntfy channel as the form has it. A secret left out is the saved
one (the token only while the topic URL's server is the saved one).

url.description: The topic URL; without it, the saved one.

OkResponse.description: The body of a write that has nothing else to say.

scope.description: Applies only to what this query matches; null = everything.

Overview.description:
`GET /filters`: the rule set, switches and lists, as the Filters &
Safety screens show them.

packs_seeded_over_rules.description:
Pack versions were first recorded at this time on a store that
already had rules (an upgrade from before versions existed, or
every version row lost): worth a notice.

pending_floor_removals.description:
Entries a config file or a floor-marked list dropped, still blocked
until you settle them (§2.7).

pending_pack_versions.description: Pack-rule versions waiting to be accepted, with their changelogs.

OverviewResponse.description:
The overview (§10.9.2): status, movement, the funnel, segments,
exceptions and Serve, for one range.

annotations.description:
Trend annotations in the range, oldest first, at most 1,000
(`/insights/events` says when there were more). Event time.

exceptions.description: What needs attention now, whatever the range (§10.9.2 level 5).

funnel.description:
The discovery cohorts in the range that have any count, oldest
first: hours up to 7 days, UTC days beyond (`range.bucket`).

funnel_total.description: The funnel over every cohort in the range.

ingest_per_hour.description:
Torrents newly stored in the last full UTC hour (§10.12). Event
time. Null when that hour wasn't measured (the crawler paused or
not running) and stored nothing.

previous.description:
The period of equal length just before, in the same shape;
present only with `compare=1`, and never for `all`.

oneOf.description:
Null while nothing identifying is recorded (the Overview then loads
no banner code).

Set when the rollups haven't been flushed for over 2 minutes
(§10.9.6); null when fresh.

trend.description:
Movement, one point per bucket (`range.bucket`), oldest first.
Event time.

updated_at.description: When the numbers were read (unix seconds).

PackAcceptance.description:
What accepting one pending pack-rule version does (RP-3). Torrent
counts are distinct torrents in the replay window whose shadow result
(the pending version beside the applied one) was recorded.

applied.description:
The version this install applied; null when it isn't known, or it
never applied the rule (a new rule).

direction.description:
The recorded direction from `applied` to `version`, every step
combined: `widens`, `narrows`, `action-heavier`, `action-lighter`
or `mixed`; null when there's no record.

disagreements.description: Torrents whose shadow result contradicts the recorded direction.

heavier.description: Torrents both versions hold, the new one with a heavier action.

in_doubt.description:
The version state is in doubt for this rule (a Filters & Safety
notice about pack versions): accepting is weakening.

lighter.description: Torrents both versions hold, the new one with a lighter action.

newly_held.description: Torrents only the new version holds.

no_longer_held.description: Torrents only the applied version holds.

review_quarantine.description:
Holds of this rule acceptance leaves for review: in quarantine, and
dropped. Nothing is released.

version.description: The version accepted: the one this build ships.

PackCorpus.description:
The pack corpora this build ships, run against its pack rules, each
rule on its own (RP-1): the same pass or fail CI enforces.

error.description: The corpus didn't load: why. Nothing else is reported then.

failures.description:
Each failure, readable: a wrong example, too few examples, a
recorded direction the corpus doesn't show.

passes.description: Everything passed (known gaps don't fail it).

precision_failing.description:
Precision items (legitimate torrents each guard exists for) held by
a rule they shouldn't be, known gaps aside.

direction_disagreements.description:
Versions of the rule whose recorded direction the corpus doesn't
show (RP-1's direction checks).

gaps.description:
Precision items the rule holds because a guard it should have
isn't built yet (a known over-filter, not a pass).

version.description: The version judged: the one this build ships.

PackOverrideState.description: Your override of one pack rule, as stored and as it applies now.

action.description: Null when the stored row doesn't read.

base.description:
The version it was made against (0: not known then); null when it
doesn't read.

changed.description:
The base rule changed since it was set (§20.8): a newer version was
accepted, or the version state is in doubt.

paused.description:
Changed, and it would weaken the rule as it is now: the rule
applies as built until the override is set again with the password.

unreadable.description:
The stored row doesn't read: the stronger of its action and the
rule's applies, and its `unless` is dropped.

action.description:
The action that applies now: the base action, or your override's
where it applies.

applied.description:
The version this install accepted; null when it isn't known, or it
never applied the rule (a new rule waiting to be accepted).

base_action.description: The rule's own action as the versions that apply now take it.

base_changed.description: Your override's base changed since you set it (§20.8).

pack_override.description:
Your override of the rule (RP-2), when it has one. Not one of the
Override entries (`overrides`), which skip rules altogether.

pending.description: The version waiting to be accepted, run in shadow meanwhile.

version.description: The rule's version as this build ships it.

changelog.description:
The pack's changelog as this build ships it (Markdown, one
`## RULE@version` entry per version, newest first).

version.description: The pack's version: its rules' versions as this build ships them.

ParseResponse.description: `GET /parse`: the AST and the canonical text it prints as.

natural.description:
With `natural=true`: the query `q` means as natural phrasing, for
the UI to preview as chips. Nothing applies it.

PasswordRequest.description:
`POST /password`: ends every other session.
`Debug` redacts the secrets.

from.description:
Unix seconds: when it paused (before the range if it was already
paused then).

to.description: When it resumed; null while still paused.

PendingFloorEntry.description: Floor entries one source dropped, waiting for a decision (§2.7).

hashes.description: Up to 1,000 of them, 40 hex digits each.

name.description: The file's path, or the list's name.

PendingInstall.description: A version in probation after an install or a rollback.

PendingPackVersion.description:
A pack-rule version waiting to be accepted (RP-0, §20.10): it runs in
shadow until `accept_pack_versions` accepts it.

applied.description:
The version this install applied; null when it isn't known, or it
never applied the rule.

changelog.description:
The changelog entries from `applied` (exclusive) to `version`,
newest first.

direction.description:
The recorded direction from `applied`, every step combined; null
when there's no record.

Policy.description: The policy in effect, as the settings and the clock make it.

held_in_process.description:
A pause failed to save (or the saved state couldn't be read at
start, notice `updater_unreadable`), so automatic installs are
held in this process only, until a pause or resume is saved or
Lodestar restarts. Releases then show `blocked_by` `held`.

next_window_at.description: When the window next opens (or now, while it's open).

paused_until.description:
Updates are paused until then: the saved pause only, never a
pause that failed to save.

security_fixes.description:
Whether security fixes install automatically (the effective
"Always install security fixes").

window_zone.description:
The zone the window is in: an IANA name, or `UTC` when none was
found on the host.

PortFamily.description: The IP family of a port range, as `netsh int <family>` names it.

PortPressure.description:
An `ephemeral_ports` exception's detail (architecture §11): Windows'
dynamic port range for one IP family, and the range to set instead.
The fix is `netsh int <family> set dynamicport tcp start=<fix_start>
num=<fix_count>`, run in a Command Prompt opened as administrator.

fix_start.description:
The range to set: its first port and how many. Null when no range
is large enough; then lowering the crawler's intensity is the fix.

needed.description:
About what Lodestar's `max_sockets` fetches and the rest of the PC
need (2,048 ports are kept for other programs).

reserved.description:
Ports inside it that other software reserved (Hyper-V, WSL,
Docker Desktop).

start.description: The dynamic range now: its first and last port.

Preview.description:
What a change would do (§20.10). Counts come from the review queue,
the tombstones, the filter hits of the replay window and the index.

Fields are in the order `POST /filters/preview` has always sent them;
where an assessment is nested in another body, its keys are sorted.

caught_30d.description: Decisions in the replay window by the rules it affects.

core_caught_30d.description: Of those, by the child-safety core.

estimate.description:
Counts from names only (sealed names, no file lists), so files'
evidence isn't re-checked: treat as an estimate.

quarantine.description: Quarantined items it would release now.

removed_from_floor.description: Entries that would leave the locked floor.

stored.description: Stored items whose hide, demote or flag mark it would clear.

tombstones.description: Dropped items it would let be fetched again.

PreviewEstimate.description: A consequence the preview can put a number on, for the UI to format.

name.description:
What it measures: `sockets` (concurrent metadata fetches), `url`
(where the UI will be after a restart), `memory_mib`.

PreviewWarning.description: Something worth knowing before saving; it doesn't stop the save.

example.message: Search stops after the restart, until you turn it back on.

PreviousKpi.description: The KPIs over the previous period.

searchable.description:
Searchable at the period's end: the last hourly snapshot in the
day before it ends. Null when there's none (search off, or not
running then).

PreviousPeriod.description: The previous period, for Compare: the fields that depend on the range.

segments.description:
The previous period's segments, in the same shape and with the
same Adult rule.

PreviousStages.description: The stage strip over the previous period.

PrivacySummary.description:
Whether something that identifies torrents or people is being recorded
now (§10.10.7 Privacy, §10.10.12), for the Overview's banner. Booleans
and a time only: never which kinds, a path, a query or a name. Read at
each request, never cached with the rollups.

identifying_until.description:
When the log stops writing data kinds that identify torrents or
people (the opt-ins included): -1 not until turned off, else Unix
seconds. Null while none is on.

query_logging.description: Searches are being saved for Insights (`insights.query_logging`).

Provenance.description:
A torrent's provenance (architecture §18.5, §18.6, §18.8).

**Private sources (§18.7):** a source with the account consent class
(Prowlarr, Jackett, private-tracker announces, your own download
clients), claims that came through a private source, and every
source of a `private_source` torrent are shown only to the signed-in
admin session. Any other caller (an API key, once these routes take
one) gets them left out (a public source with a private claim keeps
its name, with `claim` null) and `withheld` set.

network.description: The network tier (§18.6): `bt` for every stored torrent.

sources.description:
The sources that found it: the first one first, then by id.
Empty for a torrent stored before provenance was recorded.

verified.description:
It has verified metadata (§18.5). Always true here: a torrent's
detail is its BEP 9 info dictionary.

withheld.description:
Sources or claims were left out because they're private and this
caller isn't the admin session.

ProvenanceSource.description: One source that found a torrent.

oneOf.description:
How what it claimed compares with the verified metadata; null when
it made no claims about this torrent.

first_seen_at.description:
When it first found the torrent: the torrent's discovery time for
the first source; null for the others, whose first sighting isn't
recorded.

id.description: The source's id, as `GET /sources` lists it.

name.description:
The plugin's display name; its manifest id when this build doesn't
run that plugin.

plugin.description: The manifest id, as `source:` takes it.

private.description:
A private source, or its claims came through one (§18.7). Only the
admin session ever sees one.

allowed_users.description: Empty: any user the proxy names.

forced_off.description:
`LODESTAR_PROXY_AUTH=off` turned proxy auth off for this run; the
saved settings shown here don't apply until it's removed.

header.description: The header the proxy names the signed-in user in.

trusted.description: The proxies whose header is believed, as canonical CIDRs.

allowed_users.description: At most 64 user names; empty allows any.

trusted.description: IP addresses or CIDR ranges, at most 64. Required to turn it on.

PurgeJob.description:
What a purge job reports besides its progress. Every count is of
changes already saved: a purge that stopped (cancelled, failed, or cut
short by a restart) did exactly this much, and the source stays off
until a purge run again finishes it.

kept.description: Torrents others found too, kept without this source.

keys_dropped.description: Keys waiting to be fetched that were dropped.

snapshots_left.description:
Warnings the snapshot pass raised: every problem it met (a
snapshot it couldn't read or write now, one of a schema it doesn't
know, a file it couldn't delete), so this counts problems, not only
snapshots left unscrubbed. The hourly pass tries again, and a
rollback scrubs a snapshot before restoring it.

snapshots_scrubbed.description:
Snapshots the pass changed: its credentials and consent removed,
with anything else the pass was due to remove.

torrents_deleted.description: Torrents only this source found, deleted.

unverified_deleted.description: Items without metadata only this source found, deleted.

PurgePreview.description:
`GET /sources/{id}/purge/preview`: what purging the source would
remove if it ran now, counted with the purge's own rules. Nothing is
changed. The dialog shows it before you commit (§10.10.7).

While the source is off (`settled`), a purge started next removes
exactly this, as long as nothing else changes the store meanwhile. An
enabled source keeps finding until the purge turns it off, so the purge
may remove more. Keys still in memory waiting to be fetched aren't
counted: the purge reports them as `keys_dropped`.

claims_deleted.description: Claims of stored torrents it made, deleted.

kept.description:
Torrents others found too, kept without this source (`kept` in the
purge job).

queue_deleted.description: Keys it queued to be fetched, saved across restarts, dropped.

settled.description:
The source is off, so nothing it finds can add to the counts
before the purge runs.

state_deleted.description: Its plugin's saved state entries, deleted.

torrents_deleted.description: Torrents only this source found, deleted.

unverified_deleted.description: Items without metadata only this source found, deleted.

unverified_kept.description: Items without metadata others found too, kept without this source.

password.description: The admin password, checked fresh: a purge can't be undone.

adult_hold.description:
Held only because you relabelled it adult (a correction or a
classification rule) and the Adult-only core caught it: at
`expires_at` it becomes a tombstone rather than being released.

expires_at.description: When its sealed name is deleted and its quarantine ends.

pack_review.description:
An acceptance of a newer version of its pack rule left it for
review: the version that applies now may not hold it (RP-3).

QueryRow.description: A logged query and how often it ran (Serve, when query logging is on).

zero.description: Of those runs, how many found nothing.

Queue.description:
`GET /filters/queue`: quarantine (never with names) and the replay
window's decisions per rule.

next_cursor.description: The next page of quarantine, if there is one: pass as `cursor`.

RebuildEvent.description:
`event: rebuild`: index rebuild progress (§8, the "Index rebuilding"
banner of §10.4), sent when it changes, and once more with `done`.

done.description: Torrents in the new index so far.

unavailable.description: Fields that match nothing until the swap.

RebuildPhase.description: A rebuild's phase; `done` once the new index serves.

ReleaseInfo.description: A release newer than the running version.

notes.description: Signed text; render as plain text or sanitised Markdown.

name.description: `companions/<id>` for the folder; the row key for a setting.

RemovalPlan.description:
Exactly what removing a companion deletes: shown first, and returned
again once it's done.

removed.description: Whether it has been removed (`POST`), or is only shown (`GET`).

RemoveRequest.description:
`POST /companions/{id}/remove`: `confirm` is the companion's id, typed
or echoed. Anything else is `409 confirmation_mismatch`.

RestartAccepted.description:
`POST /system/restart`: accepted; the server restarts once this
answer has gone out.

estimated_seconds.description: About how long until it answers again.

Seconds this run took from start to listening: about how long a
restart pauses crawling.

hint.description: When it isn't available, how to restart instead.

ResyncEvent.description:
`event: resync`: events were missed; refetch what the page shows, then
carry on with the events that follow. It has no `id:`.

RevealRequest.description:
`POST …/reveal`: the admin password, entered again (Q5). Asked every
time, never remembered.

RevealedCredential.description:
One stored credential, in the clear: the reveal's response alone
carries it, with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

RollbackInfo.description:
Whether Roll back is offered (§10.10.7's Danger zone): this is the
"can roll back" the Updates screen shows.

lost_torrents.description:
Torrents a rollback would lose, when the store would be restored;
null when it can't be counted.

reason.description:
Why not, when `available` is false: `not_supervised`,
`image_mode`, `busy`, `no_previous_version`, `snapshot_missing` or
`not_built_yet` (Windows: Roll back isn't built for this install
yet), or the `unavailable` reason. Always sent; not `required` in the
schema yet, so clients built before it still type-check.

restores_store.description:
Whether a rollback replaces the store with the snapshot taken
before this version upgraded its schema (`false`: the store is
kept as it is). Sent when Roll back's check found the version to
roll back; absent otherwise. The snapshot is verified only when
the rollback begins.

confirm.description:
Must be true: the dialog that showed what a rollback loses was
confirmed (§10.10.7, a destructive action).

action.description: Null for an action code this server doesn't know.

shadow_until.description: Shadow mode ends then: until then it only records what it would do.

channel.description: The update channel this installation follows.

image_version.description:
The container image's (the supervisor's) own version, when it
differs: "Image 0.5.2 · running 0.5.3 (updated in place)".

overlay.description: It runs an installed update rather than the image's own code.

revoked_key.description: Its signing key was revoked after it was installed.

withdrawn.description:
Its release has been withdrawn: Roll back is offered, never done
silently.

Sample.description: One example torrent for `POST /filters/test`, never stored or logged.

type.description: A content type (`movie`, `adult`, …), replacing the classifier's.

SampleFile.description: A sample's file: a path, or a path and its size.

SamplingBlocked.description:
Why the DHT holds back its samples after a start (CR-0d): an unclean
restart, the restart proof switched off, or a restart record it can't
write.

remaining_s.description:
Seconds until sampling may begin (`dht_sample_suppression_seconds`).
For `invalidate_failed`, and `locked` while the lock is busy, it's a
lower bound: sampling also waits until the restart record can be
written.

alert.description: Alert in the app about new hits.

oneOf.description: A query AST, as `/parse` returns it.

q.description:
The query text. Send `q` or `ast`, not both; with neither it
matches everything.

rss.description: Serve the hits as an RSS feed.

SavedSearchPatch.description:
`PATCH /saved-searches/{id}`: any subset; absent leaves a field as it
is (the notifier's channels too).

paused.description:
Pausing and resuming is a toggle; resuming skips what was
indexed meanwhile.

SavedSearchView.description:
A saved search with what the list view shows beside it. The
notifier's channels and the watermark are not part of it.

alert.description: Alert in the app about new hits.

last_alert_at.description: When the newest alert was recorded; null before the first.

paused.description: Skipped by the notifier; its channels are kept.

rss.description: Serve the hits as an RSS feed.

sort.description: The sort the results open with; null = relevance.

SearchExplain.description:
How a first page was ranked (`?explain=1`, architecture §8). Field
names are stable. Relevance is `(phase1 + phase2.name + phase2.title)`
times each of `priors` (to float rounding); a prior the ranking
doesn't apply is null, and counts as 1. The other phase-2 features
aren't part of ranking yet and are null.

hits.description: One per hit, in the hits' order.

ranked_by.description:
`relevance`, or the field the hits are sorted by (`discovered`,
`size`, `files`, `seeders`, `leechers`, `trackers`, `seen`), when
no hit has relevance parts.

two_phase.description:
Whether phase 2 re-ranked the phase-1 candidates: the query has
unfielded words, or the server ranks with the swarm priors.

SearchField.description: One field of the query language.

aliases.description: Other names for it, which parse the same (`age` for `discovered`).

facetable.description:
`/facets` counts its values as a term facet. The histograms
(`size`, `discovered`, `year`) aren't term facets: false.

operators.description: How a value can be written after `name:`.

values.description:
The values it takes, when they're a fixed list (for `share`, the
file categories); absent when it's open.

SearchFieldsResponse.description:
`GET /search/fields`: the fields the query language accepts, for the
query Builder (§8, §10.4), in the parser's order.

SearchHit.description:
One search result: the torrent summary (`docs/metrics.md` §7.1), its
relevance and, for a query with a file clause, the files that matched.

composition.description:
What the torrent is made of, by colour group, in the composition
bar's order; groups without files are left out, and it's empty
before classification.

hash_v2.description: 64 hex digits; null for a v1-only torrent.

junk_reasons.description:
Stable reason keys (`docs/metrics.md` §7.1); empty when there are
none or before classification.

matched_files.description:
Positions in the torrent's file list; present only when the query
has a file clause.

resolved_via.description:
How the title was found when the name wasn't informative:
`files`, `folder` or `structure`; null = from the name itself, or
not classified.

seeders_approx.description: No tracker reported: the counts are the DHT's estimate (show ≈).

source.description:
The source that found it first, or the first one this caller may
see (§18.7: a private source is shown only to the admin session).
On `/search` hits only, and absent when none is known or visible.

swarm_suspect.description: One tracker reports a swarm nothing else sees (§8): fake seeding.

title.description: The resolved title; null = not resolved.

trackers_checked.description:
Trackers that answered in the last answered round; null = never
scraped.

trackers_reporting.description: Of those, trackers that reported anyone; null = never scraped.

verified.description:
It has verified metadata (§18.5, the "Unverified" badge when
false). On `/search` hits only.

SearchIndexState.description:
`GET /search/state`: the index's size, growth and rebuild, for the
search page's "Cold start" and "Index rebuilding" states (§10.4).

cold_start.description:
Fewer than 1,000 searchable torrents: the full-page "The index is
still growing" state (§10.19).

growing.description:
Fewer than 1,000,000 searchable torrents: the "still growing"
banner (decision S-search-2a).

growth_hours.description:
Hours of the last 24 whole UTC hours the index was measured in
(`COVERAGE` seconds on its index dim, `docs/metrics.md` §7.7),
which `growth_per_hour` averages over.

growth_per_hour.description:
Torrents that became searchable in the last 24 whole UTC hours
(the `NEWLY_SEARCHABLE` rollup), per hour of `growth_hours`; null
when nothing was measured.

oneOf.description: The rebuild under way; null when none is.

unavailable.description:
Fields the serving index lacks: clauses on them match nothing
until a rebuild adds them.

unpopulated.description:
Every field the serving index can't fully answer for: the
`unavailable` ones (as `missing`), then those nothing fills yet
and those being filled in, with how far along.
Always sent; optional in the schema so older clients and
fixtures stay valid.

updated_at.description: Unix seconds these numbers were read.

SearchLiveEvent.description:
`event: search_live`: one of your live queries (`POST /search/live`)
has new matches. `matched` counts every match since it was made, so
a missed event loses nothing. Each connection gets at most one per
live query every 5 s; counts in between are combined. Sent only to
the session that made it, never replayed (it has no `id:`), and only
torrents search would show count: none a filter rule hid (unless the
query asked for them) and no Adult while "Show adult content" is off.

matched.description: Matches since the registration was made; at least 1.

through.description:
The highest torrent id checked so far. **Null while Adult is
hidden** (see `SearchLiveRegistration.since`).

SearchLiveRegistration.description:
A live query's registration: listen for `search_live` events with
its `id` on `/events?topics=search_live` (or every topic).

id.description: Names it in `search_live` events and in `DELETE /search/live/{id}`.

since.description:
The highest torrent id searchable when it was made: matches are
counted after it. **Null while Adult is hidden**, as `torrents`'
`max_id` is: a real id would show, in its gap from a later one,
how many hidden torrents arrived.

SearchLiveRequest.description:
`POST /search/live`: the query whose new matches to count, as `/search`
takes it.

oneOf.description:
A query AST, as `/parse` returns it; it must be one the parser
could produce.

hidden.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3), as `/search` does.

q.description: The query text. Send `q` or `ast`, not both.

tz.description:
The user's zone for `time:`, in minutes east of UTC (−840 to 840);
0 by default.

SearchNotice.description: A note on what a search left out.

SearchRecovery.description:
Zero-result recovery: up to [`MAX_CLAUSES`] top-level clauses of the
query (the `of` of a root `and`), each with the total the
query has without it, counted on the same snapshot and with the same
visibility as the search (filter-hidden torrents and Adult stay out
as they did; removing `adult:…` or `hidden:…` never brings them back).

[`MAX_CLAUSES`]: lodestar_search::recovery::MAX_CLAUSES

skipped.description:
Top-level clauses past the 8 counted (filters are counted before
free text), left out.

SearchRequest.description:
`POST /search`'s body, and `GET /search`'s parameters (where `ast` is
refused: send an AST with POST).

oneOf.description:
A query AST, as `/parse` returns it; it must be one the parser
could produce.

cursor.description:
The previous page's `next_cursor`, to read the next page from the
same index snapshot. Send the same `q` (or `ast`), `sort` and
`hidden` with it.

exact.description:
Count every match exactly, even above 100,000 (within a time
budget; `total_approx` says whether it made it). `1` or `true`.

hidden.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3).

offset.description: `offset + limit` may not pass 10,000. Not with `cursor`.

q.description: The query text. Send `q` or `ast`, not both.

sort.description:
`relevance` (the default), or `discovered`, `size`, `files`,
`seeders`, `leechers`, `trackers` or `seen` with an optional `+`
(ascending) or `-` (descending, the default). Never-scraped
torrents sort last either way.

tz.description:
The user's zone for `time:`, in minutes east of UTC (−840 to 840);
0 by default.

canonical.description: The query as the server understood it.

explain.description: Present only when asked for with `explain`.

incomplete_fields.description:
The fields this query's clauses name that the index can't fully
answer for yet, when `notices` has `fields_incomplete`; empty
otherwise.
Always sent; optional in the schema so older clients and
fixtures stay valid.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page, read from the same index
snapshot (§8); null on the last page. Opaque, URL-safe, at most
256 characters, valid for 10 minutes after its last use.

notices.description:
What the server left out of these results, for the UI to say:
`adult_hidden` when the query asks for Adult (`type:adult`,
`adult:…`) while "Show adult content" is off, so it matched
nothing adult (§20.9); `fields_incomplete` when a clause names a
field still being filled in (see `incomplete_fields`).

recovery.description:
Present only on a first page with no matches whose query has two
or more top-level clauses: what removing each would give (§10.4
"No results").

stemmed.description:
Few exact matches: plural forms in titles were included too (§8),
ranked after the exact ones.

total.description: Matches in all, not just this page.

total_approx.description:
`total` is an estimate (above 100,000 matches; shown with "≈");
ask with `exact` for the exact count.

restart_required.description:
Fields whose saved value differs from the running one: they take
effect at the next restart.

revision.description:
Goes up by one with every save that changes the section. Send it
back as `if_revision` to refuse a save over someone else's.

yield.description: Searchable ÷ harvested, 0–1; null when it harvested nothing.

Segments.description:
Segments (§10.9.2 level 4). Rows are sorted by value, descending, then
key. Adult is left out entirely while "Show adult content" is off.

by_content_type.description:
Newly searchable by content type (`movie`, `tv`, …, `adult`, and
`unclassified` for none yet). Event time.

by_group.description:
The same by the content type's group: `video` (movie, tv, video),
`audio` (music, audiobook), `documents` (ebook, comic),
`software` (software, game), `images`, `other`, `adult`,
`unclassified`. Event time.

by_source.description:
Yield by the source that found each hash first, over final
cohorts. Discovery cohort.

Serve.description:
Serve (§10.9.2 level 6). Every field is null until its counter exists:
searches and latency with #48, alerts with B9, sends with the
integrations' counters.

zero_result_rate.description: Searches that found nothing ÷ searches, 0–1; null with no searches.

ServeResponse.description:
`GET /insights/serve`. Every count is null until the search, alert,
notification and send counters exist.

top_queries.description:
Most frequent queries, only with query logging on (it's off by
default, and nothing logs queries yet): null.

SettingField.description: One field of a section, for its form.

env.description: The environment variable that overrides it; null when none does.

help_key.description: Message key of the help text beside the field.

label_key.description: Message key of the field's label.

read_only.description: Never editable in the app (e.g. the data directory).

restart_required.description: A change takes effect at the next restart.

SettingSource.description:
Where a setting's effective value comes from, lowest to highest:
the built-in default, `config.toml`, a change saved in the app, or a
`LODESTAR_*` environment variable.
