env.description: The variable that set it when `source` is `env`; null otherwise.

read_only.description:
Can't be changed in the app: set by the environment, or never
editable here.

restart_required.description: A change takes effect at the next restart.

secrets_set.description:
For a list whose items hold credentials (a download client's
password): which are set, as `<item id>.<key>`. The values are
never sent. Left out when empty.

value.description: Any JSON value, of the type the section's schema gives the field.

SettingsBatch.description:
`PATCH /settings` and `POST /settings/preview`: patches for several
sections, `{section: {field: value}}`, each as `PATCH
/settings/{section}` takes it. Saved all together or not at all.

code.description: A stable snake_case identifier to branch on.

message.description: A sentence for people. It never repeats a secret's value.

SettingsErrorEnvelope.description:
A refused settings change: the API's error envelope, plus the
`section` at fault and, for `409 stale_revision`, the current values
of every section that changed meanwhile.

current.description:
On `409 stale_revision`: each stale section's values now, to merge
the edit with.

SettingsEvent.description:
`event: settings`: a section was saved (by any tab, device or API
client) and is now at `revision`. It carries no values: fetch them
with `GET /settings/{section}`.

confirm_adult.description:
The 18+ confirmation, needed when the file turns on an adult
setting (as `PATCH /settings/content` needs it).

revisions.description:
The sections' revisions the dry run reported: the import is refused
with `409 stale_revision` if any changed since.

toml.description: The file's text (TOML), at most 64 KiB.

SettingsPatch.description:
`PATCH /settings/{section}`: some of the section's fields and their
new values, as its schema in `GET /settings` describes. Fields left
out keep their values; an unknown field is refused. `null` resets a
field: its saved value is removed, and the `config.toml` value or the
default applies again.

Two keys aren't fields and are never saved: `if_revision` (the
section's `revision` the edit started from; a save over a newer one is
refused with `409 stale_revision`) and a section's confirmations
(`content`'s `confirm_adult`).

SettingsPreview.description:
`POST /settings/preview`: what a `PATCH /settings` with the same body
would do, without saving it.

SettingsSection.description: One section: its fields and the JSON schema of its values.

schema.description:
A JSON Schema (2020-12) object for the section's values, with
each number field's bounds as `minimum`/`maximum`.

allOf.description: Log in to a download client and ask its version.

oneOf.description: Log in to a download client and ask its version.

allOf.description: Ask a Torznab endpoint for its capabilities.

oneOf.description: Ask a Torznab endpoint for its capabilities.

allOf.description: Send one test message to ntfy.

oneOf.description: Send one test message to ntfy.

allOf.description: Send one test message to Discord.

oneOf.description: Send one test message to Discord.
Send one test email.

allOf.description: Post one test payload to the webhook.

oneOf.description: Post one test payload to the webhook.

SettingsTest.description: `POST /settings/test`: what to test, with the values on screen.

message.description: A sentence for people; never the URL or a credential.

example.message: The client refused the user name or password.

SettingsTestResult.description:
`POST /settings/test`: the result, shown beside the button. Nothing is
saved either way.

api_version.description: The client's API version, when it has one apart from its version.

oneOf.description: Why it failed; null when `ok`.

version.description: The client's version, as it reports it; null unless `ok`.

SetupRequest.description:
`POST /setup`: claims the instance.
`Debug` redacts the secrets.

notice_version.description:
The Legal Notice version shown and accepted (`GET /legal/notice`).
Missing or not the current one: `409 notice_required`.

token.description:
The one-time token printed to the logs (`XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`, any
case).

SiblingsResponse.description:
`GET /torrents/{hash}/siblings`: the torrents related to one, in three
groups. Each is either available (possibly empty) or unavailable with
a reason.

hash.description: 40 hex digits: the torrent asked about.

identical_payload.description:
Identical-payload clones: the same content under another hash
(equal payload signatures, confirmed by the stored file sizes).

identical_payload_partial.description:
The index is still filling in payload signatures, so some clones
may be missing from `identical_payload`.

oneOf.description:
What other versions were matched on; null when the torrent has no
parsed title.

other_versions.description:
Other versions of the same work (other releases, qualities,
groups), best first.

same_file.description:
Other torrents containing one of this torrent's files, by v2
piece root: only v2 and hybrid torrents have them
(`needs_v2_files` for a v1-only torrent).

same_file_capped.description:
The lookup was bounded: only this torrent's largest files were
looked up (it has more than the server checks), or more torrents
shared them than were read. Some may be missing from `same_file`.

same_file_partial.description:
The file index is still filling in piece roots, so some torrents
may be missing from `same_file`.

Source.description: One source plugin of this build.

agents.description: A source's concurrency, in the plugin's own unit (§18.4).

enforced.description:
Whether the running source follows `count`. Always false in this
version: it's saved and shown, and the scheduler applies it in a
later version. Label it "not active yet".

max.description: The most the plugin allows; 1 means it can't be changed.

oneOf.description:
A companion a source waits for (§18.10): it isn't started, or is
paused, until the companion is there and healthy.

companion.description:
The companion's catalogue id, such as `prowlarr` or `qbittorrent`
(for a source any download client satisfies, the suggested one).

state.description: Why a source waits for its companion.

companion_need.description:
The companion it waits for before it runs (§18.10); null when it
needs none, or has it and it's healthy. Not the same as `needs`,
which is what enabling it asks for.

config_schema.description:
The JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of its settings, as its plugin
declares it: the settings form is generated from it, and `config`
in `PATCH /sources/{id}` is checked against the plugin's own rules
(when `editable` lists `config`). Read-only, and the same for every
install: it holds no setting's value. Secrets are never in it: they
are `credential_spec`'s.

consent_required.description:
Its class is enabled by acknowledging what's shown (`external`,
`restricted`, `overlay`).

This build refuses to enable any source whose class isn't `none`
(`400 invalid_setting` on `enabled`), this one included, whatever
the request sends: it can't show its consent text yet. Once a
later version shows the class's consent text, enabling a source
with this set sends `"consent"` naming the class and
`"consent_version"`, unless that version is already acknowledged.

consent_version.description:
The version an acknowledgement must name, sent back as it is. It
holds the class's consent-text version and every address in
`endpoints`, so it changes when either does, and then the source
asks again. Empty for `none` and `account`.

credentials.description:
The names of its stored credentials; their values are never
returned.

egress.description:
A source's egress: what's set, how the running source's route is
doing, and warnings.

oneOf.description: A running source's route, as its kill switch sees it.

counts.description:
Counts since the source started (`source_egress_*` in
`docs/metrics.md`).

answered.description: Requests that got an HTTP answer.

kill_switch_aborts.description: Requests abandoned in flight because the route went down.

kill_switch_refusals.description: Requests refused before sending because the route was down.

policy_refusals.description: Requests refused by the address checks or the host list.

transport_failures.description: Requests that failed to connect, timed out or were too large.

notice.description:
What you should know about this route's privacy; null when
nothing.

reason.description: Why it's down; null when it isn't.

state.description: The live state of a source's route.

live.description:
The running source's route; null when it isn't running (a change
applies at the next start).

oneOf.description: A source's egress setting.
Who resolves names on a SOCKS5 route.

dns.description:
For `socks5`: who resolves names. Left out, it's `proxy` for a
source that only reaches its built-in sites, so lookups stay inside
the tunnel, and `local` for a source whose sites you enter, so a
public name can't reach devices on the proxy's network.

proxy.description:
For `socks5`: the proxy as `host:port` (a name, an IPv4 address or
a bracketed IPv6 address). A name is resolved when the source
starts.

setting.description:
What's saved; null when it can't be read (saved by a newer
version, or damaged). An unreadable setting is never taken as
direct: the source's requests are refused until you set its route
again.

warnings.description:
Things to fix or know, such as `HTTPS_PROXY` being set while the
source connects directly (source plugins never use it).

endpoints.description:
The addresses it contacts, as `protocol://address`, sorted: what
the consent dialog shows and an acknowledgement covers, compared
exactly. A built-in source lists hosts; one whose addresses come
from your settings (a torrent cache) lists each full address
template, path and query included, such as
`https://cache.example/~me/{hash}.torrent`. These are the
addresses it runs with now: settings saved since apply at the next
start (`restart_required`).

finds_private.description:
What it finds reflects your own setup (download clients, indexers,
Sonarr and Radarr): kept private, and never named to an API key or
feed token as a source of anything (§18.7).

oneOf.description: What enabling a source still needs (§18.7).

needs.description: What enabling it still needs; null when enabling is a toggle.

networks.description:
The networks it reaches, such as `bt`, `bt_i2p`, `ed2k`,
`ipfs` or `usenet` (§18.6).

not_yet_editable.description:
Fields `PATCH` refuses: `purge`, which runs as a job through
`POST /sources/{id}/purge`.

password_required.description:
Enabling it asks for the admin password, every time
(`restricted`, `overlay`).

priority.description: A source's share of the fetch pool (§18.4: weights 1 / 3 / 6 / 10).

purge_pending.description:
A purge started and didn't finish (cancelled, failed, or cut short
by a restart): what it removed stays removed, and the source stays
off until a purge run again finishes it.

restart_required.description:
Its stored state or saved settings differ from what's running: it
starts or picks up its new settings at the next restart. Turning
it off stops it at once: for that, this stays true only until it
has stopped.

default.description: The plugin's own windows, which apply when you haven't set any.

enforced.description:
Whether the running source keeps to `windows`. Always false in
this version: they're saved and shown, and the scheduler applies
them in a later version. Label them "not active yet".

windows.description:
The daily windows, as `HH:MM-HH:MM` in the server's local time (an
end at or before the start wraps past midnight). Empty: any time.

harvested_24h.description: Keys it was first to report in the last 24 hours.

last_error.description: Why it last stopped with an error; null when it didn't.

last_run.description:
Unix seconds it last started; null when it hasn't run since the
process started.

agents.description: Its concurrency, 1 to its `agents.max`. Applies at the next start.

config.description:
The source's settings, as its `config_schema` describes them: a
JSON object of at most 16 KiB, checked by the source's own rules
(`400 invalid_config` names the rule broken, never a value). Only
a source whose `editable` lists `config` takes it. Applies at the
next start. A torrent cache's list is `{"caches": [...]}`; a list
with an address its acknowledgement doesn't cover switches it off
at that start until you acknowledge the new list.

oneOf.description: What enabling a source requires (§18.7).

consent.description:
The consent class you acknowledge.

This build refuses to enable any source whose class isn't `none`
(`400 invalid_setting` on `enabled`), with or without this field: it
can't show its consent text yet, so nothing is acknowledged or
stored. Once a later version shows the class's consent text, this
is needed to enable a source whose `needs` is `endpoints_ack` or
`consent`, and must be its class.

oneOf.description: A source's egress setting.
Who resolves names on a SOCKS5 route.

dns.description:
For `socks5`: who resolves names. Left out, it's `proxy` for a
source that only reaches its built-in sites, so lookups stay inside
the tunnel, and `local` for a source whose sites you enter, so a
public name can't reach devices on the proxy's network.

proxy.description:
For `socks5`: the proxy as `host:port` (a name, an IPv4 address or
a bracketed IPv6 address). A name is resolved when the source
starts.

egress.description:
How its traffic leaves. Applies at the next start. Changing it
needs the admin `password` (`428 confirm_required`): a route is
what keeps a source's traffic on your VPN. `interface` and
`bind_address` are refused (`409 route_unavailable`).

priority.description: A source's share of the fetch pool (§18.4: weights 1 / 3 / 6 / 10).

purge.description: Not editable yet: refused with `409 not_editable`.

schedule.description:
Daily windows as `HH:MM-HH:MM`, at most 8; `[]` runs it any time.
Applies at the next start.

discover.description:
Unique hashes harvested in the range (first harvests: the cohorts'
harvested counts). Always approximate (≈).

fetch.description:
Metadata retrieved in the range, by event time (the writer's
flush). Null when the range starts before fetches were counted by
event time (the first whole hour after the upgrade that added it):
unknown, not 0.

index.description: Searchable torrents now; null when search is off.

serve.description:
Searches answered in the range; null until search counters exist
(#48).

understand.description: Torrents newly stored in the range. Event time.

since.description: The last flush, or the start when there was none since.

adult.description:
Adult holds made meanwhile; some may be other rules' or your
corrections'. They stay held.

dropped.description: Torrents a rule without its unreadable `unless` dropped.

kept.description:
Still held by the rules as they are, or not judged (a sealed name
that won't open).

StatsResponse.description:
`GET /stats`: what the global bar and status pill show
(`docs/metrics.md` §7.6).

data_bytes.description: Bytes the data directory holds (database, index, state).

disk_free_bytes.description:
Bytes free on the data directory's volume; null where this build
can't measure it.

fetched_per_hour.description:
Info dicts fetched per hour, over the last 5 minutes; null in the
first minute.

harvested_per_hour.description:
Keys the sources reported per hour, over the last 5 minutes; null
in the first minute.

index_lag_s.description:
Seconds the index trails the store's last commit; null when search
is off or either hasn't committed since the start.

queue_depth.description: Keys queued or in flight in the fetch pool.

oneOf.description:
Why the DHT isn't sampling yet; null when it is, before its first
report, and when it is off or not running.

searchable_torrents.description: Documents in the search index; null when search is off.

updated_at.description: Unix seconds these numbers were read.

key.description:
The DHT's strategies by name (`sample`, `get_peers`, `announce`,
`lookup`, or `strategy_<n>`), `refetch` from any source, and other
sources' own codes as `<plugin>:<n>`.

Strictness.description:
`POST /filters/strictness`: what the lists would block, and a warning
matched to it (§2.9, §20.13).

estimate.description:
Some figures are the catalog's measurements of lists not fetched
yet, and lists may overlap: a lower bound.

floor_hashes.description: Torrents a floor-marked list blocks by hash.

ipv4_public_share.description: The share of public IPv4 blocked (0–1); the level reads this.

ipv4_share.description: The share of all IPv4 blocked (0–1).

ipv6_share.description: The share of IPv6 global unicast blocked (0–1).

unknown.description: Lists never fetched, so what they block isn't known.

StrictnessBody.description:
`POST /filters/strictness`: a candidate set of lists to assess,
subscriptions by id and catalog lists by key (`lodestar lists`), in
any mix.

StrictnessList.description: One list's figures in a [`Strictness`]; null where unknown.

measured.description: The figures are a catalog measurement, not this list's data.

Subscriptions.description:
`GET /filters/subscriptions`: the one-click catalog, your lists, and
how strict the enabled ones are together (§2.9, §20.13). Nothing is
subscribed by default; connecting is `subscribe` through
`/filters/preview` and `/filters/apply`.

connected.description: Your lists, paused ones included, each with its own figures.

SuggestItem.description:
One suggestion: replace the query's characters `replace.start` to
`replace.end` (end exclusive) with `insert`. A leading `-` or `!`
stays outside the range.

count.description:
Torrents it would find, of those this search may show; absent for
field names, categories and "did you mean".

count_approx.description:
`count` is an estimate, shown with "≈" as `total_approx` is on a
search (§8): a title's past 1,000 matches, from the title set
rather than counted live.
Absent when the count is exact or there's no count.

insert.description: The query text to put in.

text.description:
What to show: the value, title or field, or for `did_you_mean`
the whole corrected query.

items.description: "Did you mean" first, then chips, field names, values and titles.

SwarmBuckets.description:
Seeders and trackers reporting, as `≥1`, `≥5`, `≥50` and
`never_scraped` values (§10.4).

SwarmSample.description:
One day or week of swarm history. Counts saturate at 65,534; null is
a gap.

at.description:
The start of the UTC day, or of the week (epoch day / 7: weeks
start on Thursday).

oneOf.description: A pending HTTP-address change; null when there is none.

channel.description: The release channel this build came from. `dev` is a local build.

connections.description: Everything Lodestar connects to, each with its state.

fixture.description:
Serving a fixture's test data (`lodestar serve --fixture`), not a
real install.

repository.description:
The source repository (`Cargo.toml`'s `repository`), so a fork
links to itself.

restart_required.description: Saved settings that apply at the next restart, as `section.field`.

TemplateRequest.description:
`POST /companions/{id}/template`: what the template is built from,
each value checked as `lodestar companion compose` checks it. Nothing
here is stored.

config_dir.description: The host folder for its settings.

downloads.description: The host folder it saves downloads in.

gluetun_container.description: The gluetun container's name, with `route: existing_gluetun`.

network.description: The Docker network Lodestar is on; `lodestar` by default.

route.description: How a templated companion's traffic leaves.

approx.description: Computed on a sample: show the counts with "≈".

distinct.description: Distinct values with a count, listed or not.

other.description:
The counts of the values not listed, summed (a torrent with two
such values counts twice).

partial.description:
The field is still being backfilled after an index upgrade, so the
counts are low (only `source`): show them as partial.

values.description:
The top values by count (ties by value), then any value the query
selects or excludes that isn't among them. Flags list `yes` and
`no`.

TestBody.description: `POST /filters/test`: a draft rule and examples to try it on.

oneOf.description: What the current rules decide; null = nothing.

draft.description: Whether the draft matches; null without a draft.

shadow.description: Rules in shadow mode that would have decided.

TitleIdentity.description:
A work's title identity (`docs/decisions/2026-10-22-B13.md`): its normalized title plus the
year, season and episode spans the release names, if any.

title_words.description:
The title's words as search tokenizes them, lowercased and
folded.

adult_hold.description: Left by an adult hold's quarantine at the 30-day purge.

pack_review.description:
An acceptance of a newer version of its pack rule left it for
review: the version that applies now may not hold it (RP-3).

Tombstones.description:
`GET /filters/tombstones`: dropped torrents, by hash and rule (no
names), so one can be found and released.

next_cursor.description: The next page, if there is one: pass as `cursor`.

Topic.description: What a client subscribes to with `?topics=`.

TorrentBody.description:
The request body: the `.torrent` file's bytes (the schema only; the
handler reads the body itself).

TorrentDetail.description:
`GET /torrents/{hash}`: the torrent summary (`docs/metrics.md` §7.1),
its swarm section (§7.2) and the first 500 files.

A null swarm field is "never scraped" (or no estimate), never 0.

adult_enrichment.description:
What an adult-enrichment service (ThePornDB, StashDB) matched
(§20.9). **Absent**, never null or empty, unless "Show adult
content" is on and the signed-in admin asks: a caller can't tell
from this field whether a match exists. Also absent for a hidden
or held torrent and for a match that came through a private
source.

dht_peers.description: BEP 33 estimate of peers (always approximate); null = no estimate.

dht_seeds.description: BEP 33 estimate of seeds (always approximate); null = no estimate.

file_list.description: The first files, in the torrent's order; the rest via `/files`.

hash_v2.description: 64 hex digits; null for a v1-only torrent.

identified_as.description:
What general enrichment identified the torrent as (ENR-10, §6):
each plugin's answer, surest first. **Absent**, never null or
empty, when there's none to show: no answer is stored, the torrent
is hidden, held, private or Adult, the host hasn't said which
sources are always adult, or every answer came from a source this
caller may not see.

provenance.description: Where it came from (§18.5, §18.8): "Found by: DHT · Nyaa".

seeders_approx.description: No tracker reported: the counts are the DHT's estimate (show ≈).

oneOf.description:
14 daily and 26 weekly samples, newest first; null = no history
kept.

swarm_suspect.description: One tracker reports a swarm nothing else sees (§8): fake seeding.

swarm_trackers.description: The trackers that reported this swarm in the last answered round.

swarm_trend.description:
Seeders per day over the last week; null = fewer than 3 daily
samples.

trackers_checked.description:
Trackers that answered in the last answered round; null = never
scraped.

trackers_reporting.description: Of those, trackers that reported anyone; null = never scraped.

TorrentsEvent.description:
`event: torrents`: torrents you can see became searchable. Commits
close together may arrive as one event. While "Show adult content" is
off, Adult torrents are left out entirely: not counted, and a commit
of only those sends no event.

added.description:
Torrents new to the index since the previous `torrents` event,
leaving out Adult while it's hidden; at least 1.

max_id.description:
The highest torrent id searchable now, while Adult is shown.
**Null while Adult is hidden:** ids are sequential, so any real id
sent beside an exact `added` would show, in its gap from the last
one, how many hidden torrents arrived. To find what's new, use the
newest id among your own results (or a cursor), not this.

TorznabDraft.description: A Torznab endpoint as the form has it, unsaved.

api_key.description:
Without it, the saved key is used if `url` is on the saved
endpoint's server.

key.description: `scheme://host:port` only: a URL path or query can carry a passkey.

TrendPoint.description:
One trend bucket. A count is null where nothing was measured (a gap:
paused, or not running), and 0 where it was measured and was 0.

harvested.description: Unique hashes first harvested in the bucket. Always ≈.

searchable.description:
Crawled torrents newly searchable in the bucket (imports
excluded).

searchable_imported.description:
Imported torrents newly searchable in the bucket; null and 0 as
for `searchable`.

Unavailable.description: Why a section isn't available. Stable keys; the UI words them.

blocked.description:
Dropped by a blocklist or filter rule before storage (counts only),
by event time; null as `fetch.kpi.fetched`.

junk_distribution.description: Junk score distribution. Null until scores are rolled up.

newly_searchable.description:
Crawled torrents that became searchable in the range, imports
excluded. Event time.

parser_confidence.description: Parser confidence distribution. Null until rolled up.

recent_corrections.description: Recent "Fix parse" corrections. Null until counted.

resolution_rate.description:
Ambiguous names resolved ÷ ambiguous. Null until a resolution
counter exists.

stored.description: Torrents newly stored in the range. Event time.

by_content_type.description:
Newly searchable by content type and group, as the overview's
segments (Adult left out while hidden). Event time.

UnpopulatedField.description:
A field the serving index can't fully answer for (architecture §8,
the population contract): `/search/state`'s `unpopulated`, and a
search's `incomplete_fields`.

done.description:
While `backfilling`: torrents with ids up to this have the field.
Null otherwise.

field.description:
The field as the query language and `/search/state` name it;
file-index fields as `file.<name>`.

upto.description:
While `backfilling`: torrents with ids in `(done, upto]` may not
have it yet; later ones do. Null otherwise.

value.description: Empty for a VPN setting you fill in yourself.

add_container_path.description:
The path on your Unraid server's web UI that opens the saved
template in Add Container.

fields.description: Label and value, in the form's order, for filling it by hand.

unread.description:
Unread alerts across every saved search, on torrents search would
show: the sum of the saved searches' `unread`.

UpdatesEvent.description:
`event: updates`: the update engine's state changed. Progress
(`bytes_done`) is sent at most once a second; fetch `GET /updates`
for the rest.

version.description: The release it concerns, when there is one.

oneOf.description:
An install under way (`now`), or one asked for at the next window
(`window`); null otherwise. It is set as soon as the install
starts, so it covers the download and verification, not only the
final install step. Progress is on the `updates` topic.
Always sent; not `required` in the schema yet, so clients built
before it (the Updates screen's fixtures) still type-check.

notices.description:
`revoked_key`, `clock_behind`, `clock_ahead`, `trust_damaged`,
`pending_unwritable`, `bad_overlay`, `rolled_back`,
`manifest_lapsed`, `channel_unavailable`, `check_not_saved` (the
last check's times couldn't be saved and won't survive a
restart), `updater_unreadable` (the saved update state couldn't be
read, so automatic updates are held; pausing or resuming saves a
new state, which rewrites the file and ends the hold) and, on
Windows, `install_failed` (the update helper's last answer, for a version
newer than the running one, wasn't `installed`; display only) and
`install_blocked` (that answer was a blocked install: Windows
wouldn't start the service, nothing changed, and the helper tries
again at the next boot unless updates are switched off or paused
first; display only) and `install_blocked_off` (the same, while
updates are already Off: switching to another mode and back to Off
cancels the retry; display only), …

oneOf.description:
Why updates aren't available at all; null otherwise. When it's
set, only `running.version` and this field mean anything: the
policy shows the defaults, and there are no releases, history or
rollback.

UpdatesUnavailable.description: Why this process has no update engine.

info_hash.description: The info dict's primary hash, as 40 hex characters.

private.description:
The info dict says `private=1` (BEP 27): stored as private, so it
never reaches the DHT, a tracker or a cache.

confirm.description:
Must be true: the dialog that showed the count was confirmed
(§10.10.7, a destructive action).

queries.description: Logged searches (only while query logging is on).

UserItemDetail.description: `GET /user-items/{hash}`: the marks and the collections it is in.

collections.description: Ids of the collections the torrent is in ("In collections").

UserItemPatch.description:
`PATCH /user-items/{hash}`: what to change. Absent leaves a mark as
it is.

labels.description:
Replaces the labels (at most 32, 1–64 characters each); an empty
list removes them.

UserItemRow.description: One marked torrent: your marks and the torrent beside them.

UserMarks.description:
A torrent's marks. Without any, `favourite` and `hidden` are false,
`labels` is empty and the rest is null.

created_at.description: Null when there are no marks.

updated_at.description: Null when there are no marks.

WebhookDraft.description: A webhook channel as the form has it.

url.description: Where the JSON is posted; without it, the saved one.

WebhookInfo.description:
One integration. The counts are since start, zero when webhooks
aren't wired.

ignored.description: Valid calls with nothing to find (Test, other events).

malformed.description: Bodies that weren't an event, dropped.

path.description: The path the app calls, under `/api/v1`.

refused.description:
Authenticated calls not delivered: over the rate, the source off,
the pipeline full, a body over the cap (`413`), or one that
couldn't be read.

token_set.description: A token is made. It can't be shown again; make a new one instead.

dropped.description:
The call was dropped: over the integration's rate, the source
turned off, or the pipeline full. Counted in `refused`.

found.description: The event named a torrent, which went to the pipeline.

token.description: Paste it into the app's webhook connection as the Password.

Worker.description:
One worker. Live values are null while it has not connected since the
coordinator started.

claimed.description: Keys claimed, as the worker last reported (its counter).

clock_offset_ms.description: The worker's clock minus the coordinator's, in ms.

clock_skewed.description: More than 60 s off (§19.3): fix NTP on the worker.

cpu_permille.description: CPU use in ‰, as last reported.

external_ips.description:
The public addresses the worker reported for itself (its egress),
at most 8. Never a peer's.

fetched.description: Metadata fetched, as the worker last reported.

id.description: The worker's id in this cluster.

last_seen_at.description: Unix seconds of its last message; null if not seen since start.

name.description:
The name it joined with (its certificate's); null when the
coordinator has no certificate on record for it.

paused.description:
Paused by the admin: it gets no new work until resumed, and stays
paused across reconnects and restarts. Set while offline too, when
`status` can only say `offline`.

processed.description: Torrents processed, as the worker last reported.

rss_mb.description: Resident memory in MB, as last reported.

spool_bytes.description: Bytes waiting in its on-disk spool (§19.6).

WorkerBudget.description: A worker's resource budget. 0 means no cap beyond the defaults.

WorkerIntensity.description: A worker's crawl intensity (§19.5: each worker has its own).

allowed.description: "Allow workers" is on and the cluster port is serving.

workers.description: Every joined worker, by id. Empty on a single machine.

WorkerPatch.description:
`PATCH /workers/{id}`: any of these; absent fields are kept. `budget`
is sent whole, all four fields.

gone_within_secs.description: Seconds until its connection is closed, at most: one heartbeat.

leases_returned.description: Leases taken back and offered to other workers.

WorkerStatus.description:
A worker's state as Settings → Workers shows it (icon + text).
`quarantined` arrives with WK-13.

WorkerTokenCreated.description:
The one response that carries a join token. It can't be read back:
only its hash is kept. `Debug` redacts the token and the commands.

token.description: The `lsj1…` token: single use, for this name only.

Error.description: Any failure: the error envelope. `error.code` is stable; branch on it.
